# DanStroke

DanStroke is a Danish clinical stroke database that formerly served as the primary data source for Indicator 5 (incidence of ischemic stroke among atrial fibrillation patients) in the annual reports of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark) [^src2]. In both the 2023 and 2024 annual reports, the reporting bodies chose to base Indicator 5 on data about acute apoplexy ("akut apopleksi") drawn from LPR (the Danish National Patient Registry) rather than from DanStroke itself [^src1] [^src3].

The stated reason for this switch was that DanStroke had been affected by gaps in the reporting of stroke cases ("manglende indberetninger af apopleksitilfælde"), a problem attributed to the database's transition to a new reporting model [^src1] [^src3]. By using LPR data instead, the report authors state that Indicator 5 is not affected by these shortcomings in DanStroke [^src1]. Despite the shift to LPR as the primary source, the 2024 report notes that a supplementary table was still included in the Appendix showing Indicator 5 as calculated from data obtained from DanStroke, preserving a parallel view of the indicator for comparison [^src3].

DanStroke's role illustrates a broader methodological issue affecting quality indicator reporting in the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database: when a source registry undergoes structural changes to its reporting model, downstream indicators dependent on it can suffer data completeness problems, prompting substitution with alternative registries such as LPR [^src1] [^src3]. This dynamic is part of the broader narrative in both the 2022–2023 and 2023–2024 annual reports concerning Indicator 5 and Indicator 6, which track ischemic stroke and intracranial bleeding incidence among atrial fibrillation patients across Denmark's five regions.
